fixes.explanation: Right, friend, no cheers. The text says they were startled and frightened, thinking they had seen a spirit (Luke 24:37). Jesus says, "Peace be with you." (Luke 24:36), and they're still startled and frightened. I think a few of them stopped breathing for a second.

It's True, friend, and here's the proof. Jesus says, "Touch Me and see…" (Luke 24:39). He invites them to check for themselves. He also says, "Why are you troubled," and "why do doubts arise in your hearts?" (Luke 24:38).

That's the reason, baker. Jesus says, "…for a spirit does not have flesh and bones, as you see I have." (Luke 24:39). He points to what they can see right in front of them. And He tells them to touch Him and see.

That's the one, baker. They gave Him a piece of broiled fish, and He took it and ate it in front of them (Luke 24:42-43). They were still in disbelief because of their joy and amazement when He asked for something to eat (Luke 24:41). Fish on the menu, and all of them watching.

Grapes would've been fancy, friend, but the text doesn't have them. It says they gave Him a piece of broiled fish. Then He took it and ate it in front of them (Luke 24:42-43). Everyone in the room watched Him eat it.

Yes, baker, Jerusalem. Jesus says it will be proclaimed to all nations, "…beginning in Jerusalem." (Luke 24:47). Earlier in this chapter, the disciples had gathered together in Jerusalem (Luke 24:33). The starting line is the city they're already in.

Galilee is a real place in the story, friend, but it's not named here. Jesus says, "…beginning in Jerusalem." (Luke 24:47). Earlier in this chapter, the disciples had gathered together in Jerusalem (Luke 24:33). So the message starts in the city they're already in.

Nazareth is a good guess for Jesus' story, baker, but Jesus doesn't name it here. He says, "…beginning in Jerusalem." (Luke 24:47). Earlier in this chapter, the disciples had gathered together in Jerusalem (Luke 24:33). So that's where the message begins, in the very city they're in.

True, baker. Jesus tells them, "You are witnesses of these things." (Luke 24:48). Right before that, He tells them what is written: the Christ will suffer and rise from the dead on the third day (Luke 24:46). I think that's a weighty job, and He puts it right on them.

No bread this time, baker. The text says, "While He was blessing them, He left them and was carried up into heaven." (Luke 24:51). Earlier, He had eaten a piece of broiled fish in front of them (Luke 24:43). But at Bethany it's a blessing, and then He's carried up.
